name: Bortezomib
route_note: SC (preferred) or IV injection, usually twice weekly or weekly in cycles
originator: ProScript/Myogenics (Julian Adams and colleagues); developed by Millennium Pharmaceuticals
owner: Takeda (Velcade); Johnson & Johnson outside US/Japan; generic (many)

discovery.by: Julian Adams and colleagues, ProScript (formerly Myogenics)
discovery.note: Dipeptidyl boronic acid designed as a reversible inhibitor of the proteasome's chymotrypsin-like site; NCI screening revealed broad antitumour activity.

tagline: First proteasome inhibitor, a cornerstone of multiple myeloma therapy
summary: Bortezomib is a reversible inhibitor of the 26S proteasome, the cell's main machinery for degrading ubiquitinated proteins. Myeloma cells, which make large amounts of immunoglobulin, are especially vulnerable; bortezomib-based combinations are standard in multiple myeloma and mantle cell lymphoma.
mechanism: The boron atom of bortezomib binds the catalytic threonine of the β5 subunit (chymotrypsin-like activity) of the 20S proteasome core, and to a lesser extent β1.

Proteasome inhibition causes accumulation of misfolded proteins and endoplasmic-reticulum stress (unfolded protein response), stabilises pro-apoptotic factors and IκB, and suppresses NF-κB signalling, leading to apoptosis. Plasma cells, with their high protein synthesis load, are particularly sensitive.
uses: Multiple myeloma (newly diagnosed and relapsed, in combinations such as VRd, VMP, VTd, D-VRd)
Mantle cell lymphoma (including first-line with rituximab-based chemotherapy)
Off-label: AL amyloidosis, antibody-mediated transplant rejection

history.title: Millennium
history.detail: Millennium Pharmaceuticals acquires the compound through LeukoSite, which had bought ProScript.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Accelerated approval for relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma (SUMMIT), the first proteasome inhibitor.

history.title: Mantle cell lymphoma
history.detail: Approval for relapsed mantle cell lymphoma.

history.title: First-line myeloma; Takeda
history.detail: VISTA leads to first-line approval; Takeda acquires Millennium.

history.title: Subcutaneous route
history.detail: SC administration approved after showing less neuropathy than IV.

history.title: SWOG S0777
history.detail: VRd (bortezomib, lenalidomide, dexamethasone) improves survival over Rd in newly diagnosed myeloma.

history.title: Generics
history.detail: Generic bortezomib becomes available in the US after patent expiry.

pk.excretion: not well characterised; renal and biliary

facts: Antiviral prophylaxis (e.g. aciclovir) is routinely given because bortezomib increases herpes zoster reactivation.
